cd8b14f826a3ba1a.question: What does the customer want, and has the bank promised anything so far?

answer.answer: The customer wants two things: the account reopened and an explanation of why it was closed. The file records no promise or commitment by the bank to the customer. The only bank note says the account was closed after a financial crime review and that the review reasons cannot be disclosed to the customer. There is no record of any contact with the customer since the complaint, nor of any offer, reopening, refund or redress. Whether to reopen the account or offer anything is for an authorised person to decide.

e3673e5776a5e259.question: Which policy rules decide this case, and what do they require the handler to do?

answer.answer: This is a complaint (CH-1): the customer is dissatisfied and alleges loss and distress (wages bounced, rent unpaid). Severity is High under CH-6 because of threatened legal action and media contact, and ESC-1 routes these to Senior Complaints Review. The handover must be made within 2 business days (ESC-2) and include all ten ESC-3 fields. The root cause tag (likely Account opening or closure, CH-7) is for the handler to confirm. The case is At risk, so a team leader must review it weekly (CH-5). Vulnerability was not asked about. The missed rent may signal financial difficulty, so the handler should ask sensitively (VUL-2) and consider a VUL-4 referral. The file holds no specific policy on account closure notice periods or on disclosing financial crime reviews. The outcome and any redress are for an authorised person (CH-8).
